tasks.instruction: Listen to a talk in an environmental science class.

questions.stem: What is the main topic of the talk?

options.A: A range of environmental issues affecting national parks
options.B: How people contribute to pollution in ecosystems
options.C: Animal species at risk of extinction
options.D: A conservation strategy to restore ecosystems

questions.stem: Why does the speaker talk about the wolves in Yellowstone National Park?

options.A: To illustrate a successful example of rewilding
options.B: To describe the typical behavior of wolves in their habitat
options.C: To illustrate how some wolf species have become endangered
options.D: To highlight the unpredictability of ecological outcomes

questions.stem: According to the speaker, what challenge is often faced by rewilding projects?

options.A: Lack of funding for wildlife reserves
options.B: Objections raised by people living near rewilding sites
options.D: Limited availability of species that can adapt to restored ecosystems

questions.stem: What is important for rewilding to succeed?

options.A: Focusing on plant restoration before reintroducing animals
options.B: Using historical records to recreate exact past ecosystems
options.C: Keeping track of wildlife and ecosystems for ongoing analysis
options.D: Prioritizing fast-growing species to speed up recovery

tasks.instruction: Listen to a talk in a psychology class.

questions.stem: What is the main topic of the talk?

options.A: Some flawed assumptions in early social psychology
options.B: How people respond to a person in need when in groups
options.D: Why people conform to social norms

questions.stem: In the 1960s experiment mentioned in the talk, what happened when participants were alone?

options.A: They waited to see if the situation would resolve itself.
options.D: Some of them went to get advice from others.

questions.stem: What are the two main psychological processes contributing to the bystander effect?

options.D: Diffusion of responsibility and social influence

questions.stem: What point does the speaker make about being aware of the bystander effect?

options.A: It can encourage people to take action.
options.B: It can make people feel less responsible.
options.D: It can result in a stronger bond with the group.
